# Postmortem - April 6 ACH Pipeline Failure

**Severity:** P0 (customer money movement delay, no financial loss) · **Reviewed by:** Marcus Bell, Aleks Varga · **Status:** Published 2026-04-14; action items tracked below

## What happened

On Sunday April 6 between 4 PM and 11 PM PT, our ACH origination pipeline stalled. The Sunday afternoon submission batch, 2,138 user auto-deposits totaling $147k, failed to reach Pillar Bank before the 6 PM PT NACHA cutoff. Affected users saw deposits delayed by 3 business days (April 7-9).

No funds were lost. No regulatory deadline was missed (a cutoff, not a regulatory deadline). Customer trust took a hit.

## Timeline (PT)

- **4:14 PM** Sidekiq workers begin processing the Sunday batch. Normal.
- **4:38 PM** Worker throughput drops to ~10% of expected. Devon Park spots it on his dashboard and pings Marcus in Slack.
- **4:45 PM** Marcus sees Redis memory pressure and worker stalls. First hypothesis: Redis OOM.
- **5:10 PM** Workers restarted. Throughput recovers briefly, then stalls again. Not Redis.
- **5:34 PM** Real cause found: NACHA file generation hung on a ~800-transaction batch. The serialization step is O(n²) on a rarely used code path.
- **5:48 PM** Fix deployed bypassing the slow path. Workers resume.
- **6:00 PM** NACHA cutoff passes. The repaired batch is too late.
- **6:12 PM** I'm paged. War room: Marcus, Aleks, Renee Alvarez, me.
- **6:30 PM** Decision: submit Monday. Users see funds Wednesday.
- **7:45 PM** Customer comms drafted; email and push out by 9 PM.
- **11:00 PM** All 2,138 users notified. Compensation approved.

## Root cause

NACHA serialization had a hot path and a cold path. The cold path triggered when more than 30% of a batch was Pillar's "modified ACH" return-on-failure type. It was O(n²) in batch size. Below ~200 such entries nobody noticed. The April 6 batch was 35% modified-ACH and 800+ entries, so serialization took minutes per transaction. Sidekiq workers timed out, retried, failed again. Cascade.

## Contributing factors

- **Untested code path.** Written 14 months earlier for a different reason, rarely exercised, no tests.
- **No batch-size monitoring.** An 800+ batch was anomalous and nothing told us.
- **Sidekiq's at-least-once semantics.** Retries amplified the problem.
- **Sunday staffing.** Devon caught it because he happened to be looking. Luck, not detection.
- **No fallback path.** When the cutoff was missed there was no runbook, just a decision under pressure.

## What we did well

- Detected within 25 minutes, root cause within an hour.
- Honest comms out within 5 hours.
- Compensation issued proactively: $25 credit to each affected user, $53,450 in total.
- Aleks and I were aligned on the response.

## What we did poorly

- Should have caught the batch size before processing began.
- Should not have had an untested O(n²) path in money movement.
- Sidekiq for ACH was known to be fragile. I knew it and didn't prioritize it.
- Compensation was decided live instead of from a runbook.

## Action items

As published on 2026-04-14:

- [x] Marcus: hotfix the O(n²) serialization by 2026-04-07
- [x] Marcus: batch-size alerts by 2026-04-08
- [x] Maya: codify customer compensation ($25 credit for any delay caused by our error) by 2026-04-10
- [x] Maya: ADR for a durable ACH pipeline by 2026-04-19 (ADR-024 - Move ACH Processing Off Sidekiq)
- [x] Maya: Sunday on-call protocol update by 2026-04-15 (On-Call Rotation Design)
- [x] Marcus: Sunday-volume load test of the new pipeline passing at 3x before cut-over by 2026-07-25
- [x] Marcus: customer-comms runbook for money movement delays by 2026-06-02
- [x] Maya: missed-cutoff protocol agreed with Pillar Bank (Theresa Lowe) by 2026-06-04
- [ ] Marcus: NACHA-cutoff alerting tuned to page before the window closes by 2026-10-13

## Status update (2026-09-18)

- ADR-024 accepted 2026-04-19. The first Sunday load test on June 27 failed at 3x volume (Sunday Load Test Results - June 27), which moved cut-over from end of June to August.
- Shadow mode ran Aug 4-17. Cut-over to the Go pipeline on 2026-08-18. Zero missed cutoffs since. See ACH Cut-over Retro.
- The customer-comms runbook shipped 2026-06-02: Runbook - Customer Comms for Money Movement Delays.
- The 30-day stability hold ended 2026-09-17 and deletion of the Sidekiq ACH code is approved (Sidekiq ACH Decommission Plan).
- [ ] Devon: delete the Sidekiq ACH code by 2026-10-16

Risk: the NACHA-cutoff alert still fires too often on normal Sunday volume (Runbook - NACHA Cutoff Alert). An alert people learn to ignore is the April 6 failure mode again.

## Lessons

1. Money movement code paths are tested or removed. Cold paths that exist "in case" are a liability.
2. Known architectural fragility compounds. I should have prioritized the fix before it bit us.
3. Monitoring is not detection. We need automated detection at the boundaries.
4. Comms speed beats message polish.

## Personal note

This is the worst engineering day of my Stencil tenure. The team handled it well. The architecture I let stand caused it. If a similar failure happens after the rebuild, the problem is no longer infrastructure. It's me.
